conventions: Possessive recasting of a relative clause with a prepositional predicate: `אֲשֶׁר קֶסֶת הַסֹּפֵר בְּמָתְנָיו` → *who had the inkhorn by his side* (9.3 s031, 9.11 s011) gives the supplied *had* to the בְּ heading that predicate under rules 43 and 49, the unit discontinuous around the object and headed on the preposition's own *by*. It is given neither to אֲשֶׁר as a possessive relative nor to the suffix on מׇתְנַיִם, which keeps *his*, and it is not `added`: dropping *had* diminishes only the possession relation, which is rule 43's test. Where the ASV writes no possessive verb for the same Hebrew — 9.2 s035, *with a writer's inkhorn by his side* — the preposition takes only its *by*.

Where the ASV writes a single English word for a multi-morpheme Hebrew expression, this chapter fused under rule 30 rather than rendering one morpheme and stranding the rest as `unrepresented`: `מֵעַל` → *from* (9.3, headed on מִן), `אֲשֶׁר … עָלָיו` → *whereupon* (9.3, headed on אֲשֶׁר, which carries the *where-*), `לְמַשְׁחִית` → *utterly* (9.6, headed on מַשְׁחִית), `בִּמְאֹד מְאֹד` → *exceeding* (9.9, headed on מְאֹד), `כַּאֲשֶׁר` → *as* (9.11, headed on כְּ). The rule 22 reading that renders one occurrence and marks the repetition unrepresented was weighed at 9.9 and rejected. Where the ASV instead spends a second English word on a particular morpheme the condition is unmet and the pair splits: `עַל … אֲשֶׁר` → *upon whom* at 9.6 s016/s017 is two units, with the resumptive suffix unrepresented.

The slaughter list `זָקֵן בָּחוּר וּבְתוּלָה וְטַף וְנָשִׁים` (9.6): each anarthrous substantive takes the ASV's supplied *the* into its own unit (rules 15, 46), and the heads follow rule 31's subtraction test rather than the English phrase's noun — `זָקֵן` → *the old man* on *old*, `בָּחוּר` → *the young man* on *young*, `טַף` → *little children* on *little*. The competing reading heads the two noun lexemes on *man* and *children*, on the ground that בָּחוּר and טַף already name their class; it is named in the verse notes and was not taken. `חֲלָלִים` → *with the slain* (9.7 s014) and `מֻטֶּה` → *wresting of judgment* (9.9 s023, italic completion included) are headed on the same principle.
report: Read all 11 verses end to end against the 35-lemma candidate table. Every multi-treatment bucket is the ASV rendering one morpheme differently in a different context, and the difference is licensed by the source or by the English actually written; no construction is analysed two ways.

Waw (37 tokens): C→Vqw3ms splits *Then*/*And*/*and* and, at 9.8 s009, *that* — the last is rule 45's middle case, the apodosis opening with its own waw while 9.8 s002 keeps only *it came to pass*. C→Ncmsa is unrepresented at 9.1 s014 and 9.2 s015 because the ASV writes no connective before *every man*, and aligned at 9.2 s023 and 9.6 s005 where it writes one. All read off the ASV per rule 14.

Article (30 tokens): the mixed Td→Ncmsa and Td→Ncmpa buckets are rule 29/47 determiner-counting, not two analyses. Unrepresented only where the ASV writes no *the* for the phrase (9.2 s033 *a writer's inkhorn*, 9.3 s023/s025, 9.6 s033, 9.11 s006 *in linen*); elsewhere the present article takes the written *the*, fronted where the rectum is rendered anarthrously (9.2 s044, 9.3 s029) and standing before its own word where it is not (9.2 s009, 9.3 s016, 9.4 s009/s019).

Lemma ה has two treatments because it is two morphemes: Sd at 9.2 s014 → *toward* (rule 32), Sh at 9.8 s011 unrepresented (rule 32's first sentence). Morphology, not a split. Likewise אֹזֶן *ears*/*hearing*, גָּדוֹל *loud*/*is great*, קֶסֶת *a inkhorn*/*inkhorn*, אִישׁ *every man*/*man*/*men*/*of men*, אָמַר *he said*/*said he* — all ASV wording over identical analyses.

Connective audit, which is what the candidate table cannot see: for each of the 11 verses I counted the ASV's connectives against the clause's waws and כִּי. Every verse balances except 9.10 t016 *but*, whose clause (דַּרְכָּם בְּרֹאשָׁם נָתָתִּי) carries no conjunction at all; that is the chapter's single `added` unit and is correct under rules 51 and 55. Nowhere else is a supplied connective folded into a morpheme that does not license it — 9.6 s012, the other clause-initial *but*, does have its waw.

Parallel constructions agree across verses: the possessive recasting *who had the inkhorn by his side* puts *had* on בְּ at both 9.3 s031 and 9.11 s011, and 9.2 s035, where the ASV writes no possessive verb, gives the same preposition only its *by*. The five object markers agree too: four unrepresented (9.7 s006/s011, 9.8 s026, 9.9 s028) where the ASV writes the object bare, one aligned to *of* at 9.8 s033 where the gerund *pouring out* reaches its object through it — rule 16's first family, and the difference is in the ASV, not in the analysis.

Source heads for the two fusions that could have gone either way — אֲשֶׁר…עָלָיו → *whereupon* headed on the relative (9.3), כַּאֲשֶׁר → *as* headed on the preposition (9.11) — are different expressions, not one construction read twice; both notes name the competing reading under rule 8.

BSB: 13 disagreements, all ASV-side unrepresented against BSB represented, and every one a documented convention difference — לֵאמֹר's לְ (rule 27, 9.1/9.11), עַל before a bare English object (rule 40, 9.6 s013), five articles the ASV writes no *the* for (rules 29/47), a resumptive suffix (rule 22, 9.6 s018), the paragogic he (rule 32, 9.8 s011), and the unrendered suffix on אֲדֹנָי (rules 18/22, 9.8 s021). None is a genuine error and no accepted edge was changed.

Promotions considered and declined: an amendment to rule 43 widening the possessive preposition to a locative בְּ heading the predicate, and one to rule 16 naming a gerund's *of*. Rule 43 already carries a non-dative example (שָׁפְרָה עָלָי → *I have*) and rule 16's first family already says an English verb may reach its object through a preposition, so both would be near-restatements, and no corpus evidence for either was in hand. Recorded as conventions instead.
